The focused host run had 153 survivors. Adapting two broader existing T3 test blocks removes 88 of them. The supplemental run has 171 assertion kills, 65 survivors and two ordinary runtime errors. These are selection gaps, not 88 newly discovered missing upstream tests.

Inspection of twenty SDK survivors identified eleven public-behavior test gaps. Direct controls confirmed that the old eleven tests pass every observed mutation and the strengthened eighteen tests fail each one. Ordinary exceptions remain runtime evidence under the conservative protocol.Inspected survivorsCountPublic test gaps11Implementation details7Equivalent under stated assumptions2

The original five-test reporter run had three framework timeouts. An unchanged retry ran a fresh baseline, reused 151 complete results and reran those three. It completed with 66 kills and 88 survivors. Selected public behavior controls have eight retained old-test PASS/new-test FAIL witnesses.ClassificationSurvivorsUseful public controls46Implementation details40Qualified equivalents2

Two Git parser runs reproduced cleanup uncertainty after a nonadvancing-loop mutation. The corrected source gives owned process groups five seconds to settle while keeping pipe drain bounded at 250 ms. Regression controls preserve ownership and fail closed. Real corrected replay and final acceptance must be checked in the handoff. CSV reuse preserves 50 complete results after a fresh baseline and reruns two genuine timeouts.
